title: P0 planar kernel: coincident/collinear edges are NOT merged → corrupt DCEL, zero faces (blue-over-blue union broken)
description:
DEFECT in the P0 curve-aware planar geometry kernel (commit ba39d0e, packages/core/src/engine/planar/). The arrangement merges coincident VERTICES (exact twip-key) but NEVER merges coincident/collinear EDGES. Inserting an edge that lies exactly on an existing edge adds a second parallel twin-pair, producing a multigraph; the rotation-system angular sort then ties (identical atan2 directions), next/prev linking breaks, face extraction collapses, and the result is a non-planar Euler value with ZERO bounded faces — the fill is entirely lost.

This is the canonical merge-model 'same-color union' (blue-over-blue) case the oracle lists (merge-drawing-oracle.spec.ts case 2) and any tiled/shared-edge artwork. All later phases (P1-P5) build on this kernel, so wrong topology here is HIGH severity.

ROOT CAUSE (arrangement.ts insertEdge): intersection splitting only registers INTERIOR params (h.tA/h.tB filtered to (1e-7, 1-1e-7), arrangement.ts:184-192). A fully-coincident edge's collinearOverlap (intersect.ts:72) reports overlap endpoints AT tA in {0,1}, which the interior filter discards → no split AND no dedup of an edge identical to an existing one. There is no 'an undirected edge between these two vertices already exists' check, and collinear-overlap of two edges (where one lies on a sub-span of the other) is not resolved into a shared edge.

PROVEN FAILING INPUTS (run via buildArrangementFromShapes; RED solid fill):

CASE A — two IDENTICAL squares (0,0,10,10) both RED:
  expected: 1 red face, area 100, euler 2.
  actual:   redArea=0, redFaces=0, undirEdges=8 (every edge DOUBLED — he0 & he8 are both (0,0)->(10,0), etc.), euler=-3, the only face is the unbounded one with holes=[0,1,2,4] and fill=null. ENTIRE FILL LOST.

CASE B — two RED squares sharing an edge: rect(0,0,10,10) + rect(0,10,10,10) (share the y=10 span x=0..10):
  actual: euler=0 (invalid planar value); area summed to 200 only by luck. Corrupt DCEL.

CASE C — hole touching outer boundary: outer RED rect(0,0,30,30) + inner BLUE rect(0,10,10,10) whose left edge x=0 is collinear with the outer left edge:
  expected: total covered 900 (red 800 + blue 100).
  actual:   total=100, redArea=0 (outer red square's area collapsed to 0). Outer fill lost when an inner edge is collinear with an outer boundary edge.

CASE D — epsilon-coincident (same root cause): two lines (0,0)->(10,0.001) and (0,0.001)->(10,0) both snap to the identical (0,0)->(10,0) segment (0.001px=0.02twip→0); result is the doubled-edge multigraph (euler=1), confirming snapping correctly collapses them to coincident edges but the kernel then fails to merge those edges.

WORKING cases (for contrast, NOT regressions): offset overlap rect(0,0,20,20)+rect(10,10,20,20) → 12 undirEdges, euler 2, correct (no two edges fully coincident). T-junction, zero-length-ignore, line-splits-fill, dangling-stroke, top-wins, large-coords, figure-8, single-arc cuts: all correct.

REPRO: buildArrangementFromShapes([rectShape(0,0,10,10,RED), rectShape(0,0,10,10,RED)]) then sum faceArea over bounded faces with fill===0 → 0 (expected 100); eulerCharacteristic → -3 (expected 2). The existing planar.test.ts happy-path suite (24 tests) misses this because every authored case avoids fully-coincident or collinear-coincident edges.

FIX DIRECTION (for implementer): when inserting an edge, detect that an undirected edge between the same two snapped vertices with the same geometry already exists and MERGE into it (union the fill/line labels) instead of adding a parallel twin-pair; AND resolve collinear partial overlaps by splitting BOTH edges at the shared sub-span endpoints (already computed by collinearOverlap, but currently dropped at the endpoints by the interior-only param filter) so the shared span becomes one edge carrying merged labels. Add adversarial regression tests for cases A-D (Euler==2, area conserved, exactly one merged face for the duplicate).

VERIFICATION CONTEXT: P0 is INERT — exported only via engine/index.ts, not imported by renderer/compiler/SWF-encode/editing. node tools/golden-parity.mjs exits 0, self-determinism 9d09912df4727d0c (4-run consistent); core 5421 pass (2 pre-existing task-1207 fixture ENOENT unrelated). So this is a kernel-correctness defect with NO current user-facing regression, but it MUST be fixed before P1 wires the kernel into live shape editing.
